loconautics.configuration.blocks.bearing: Stress multiplier for a Bearing Axle driving against the rest of its train.
loconautics.configuration.blocks.turntab: Stress Units used by a Turntable Bearing per RPM of plate speed.
loconautics.configuration.boiler.maxLeng: Most body blocks a boiler may span along its length before it stops working. Longer boilers burn more fuel and draw more water.
loconautics.configuration.compat.compute: Allows computers to control trains, signals, points and turntables by ID. Turning this off limits control to computers inside the train.
loconautics.configuration.foundation.ena: Allows stations to assemble standard Create trains.
Allows stations to assemble Loconautics physics trains.
loconautics.configuration.track.derailme: How much a collision must change a carriage's speed, in blocks per second, to derail it.
Allows coupled carriages in the same train to derail each other when they collide.
The most a curve lifts the outside wheels while derailOnCurve is off.
Off, a fast curve only lifts the wheels on the outside a little. On, curves are full physics and a car taken too fast tips off.
Allows a strong upward push, such as from a Physics Staff, to lift a train off the rails.

Upward push that lets go of the rail on a Carriage that can lean, as a share of its own weight. 0 leaves it to the wheel lift alone. Holding a Train up already costs 1.0, so keep this well above it or a staff drag throws it off.
Maximum angle in degrees that a rail can tilt away from level before a train derails.
Speed in blocks per second at and above which a leaning Carriage comes off at rollUnglueDegrees. Between the two speeds the angle blends smoothly.
Speed in blocks per second at and below which a leaning Carriage only comes off once it is really falling over.
Roll angle a fast Carriage can lean before it comes off the rail.
How far a Carriage body leans on its springs when the load sits right over one rail. The wheels stay on the rail, 0 keeps the body level.
How much a leaning Carriage wobbles before it settles. 1 settles with no bounce, lower rocks longer.
How far the wheels lift for an overturning push twice as strong as gravity can hold. Higher lifts more.
The most the wheel hinge holds a lean. A load that needs more than this tips the Carriage over.
loconautics.configuration.track.railHopM: Maximum angle in degrees between the train's heading and a rail it can hop onto.
loconautics.configuration.train.dynamics: Acceleration for a train at the reference mass.
How quickly the brakes slow a train, regardless of its mass.
Controls how strongly train mass affects acceleration. At 0, acceleration is independent of mass. At 1, it scales inversely with mass.
A train of this mass uses the base acceleration. Lighter trains accelerate faster and heavier ones more slowly.
Controls how quickly a coasting train slows down. Set to 0 to disable rolling resistance.
Adds stress to working Bearing Axles when the train climbs a slope.
Extra stress impact per degree of climb, shared by the working axles.
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_row_powe: Power and Fuel of Engine Rows
Each running engine adds 8192 Stress Units to the output
Speed is set by the slowest running engine
Fuel is shared by all engines in the row
A broken engine passes its fuel on to its neighbors
block.loconautics.small_combustion_engin: Um Motor de _seis cilindros_ que gira um Eixo, queimando _combustível líquido_ de um Balde ou Tubo.
_Desacelera_ quanto mais forte o sinal, e _para_ quando o sinal está mais forte.
Extra horizontal distance in blocks to scan beyond the station's assembly area.
How many blocks above the bogeys the station scans during assembly.
How many blocks below the bogeys the station scans during assembly.
Keeps chunks loaded around physics trains stopped at stations.
loconautics.configuration.train.visual.b: Controls how strongly bogeys shift sideways in curves as train speed increases. Set to 0 to disable sway.
Caps the sideways offset from bogey sway.
Lets bogeys use physics pivots to follow the rails.
loconautics.configuration.train.relocati: Allows players to move physics trains with a Wrench.
Limits Wrench relocation to trains that have derailed.
loconautics.configuration.track.railSear: Horizontal search radius in blocks when looking for nearby track.
Vertical search range in blocks when looking for nearby track.
loconautics.configuration.track.derailme: Allows trains to derail when they hit the end of the track.
Impact threshold for derailment when a train hits the end of the track.
Scales the drive force of a derailed train on the ground. Set to 0 to disable this movement.
loconautics.configuration.track.rerail.a: Allows trains and off-track bogeys to return to nearby rails automatically.
Maximum speed at which a train can begin rerailing automatically.
loconautics.configuration.hatch.injector: Water storage capacity of fluid hatches and supported Hullsteel sockets, in millibuckets.
loconautics.configuration.blocks.analog_: Ticks between steps toward zero throttle when the controller is unattended, unlocked and free of schedule control.
Limits the reverse throttle signal when driving with the Analog Controller.
loconautics.configuration.blocks.transmi: Stress Units used by a Transmission per RPM of output speed.
loconautics.configuration.items.steel_ca: Maximum distance in blocks between two ends of a Steel Cable.
loconautics.configuration.couplers.knuck: Ticks between scans for new knuckle coupler connections.
loconautics.configuration.hose.maxLength: Maximum length in blocks for a hose connection.
loconautics.configuration.explosions.sub: Allows explosions to push nearby Sable contraptions.
Scales the knockback radius based on the explosion's power.
Scales how strongly an explosion pushes nearby contraptions.
Adds an upward component to the explosion's knockback.
Minimum distance in blocks used in the inverse-square knockback calculation.
loconautics.configuration.explosions.dem: Base explosion power setting for Demolition Charges.
Configured limit on the number of charges.
Configured fuse delay in game ticks.
loconautics.configuration.patch.enableRo: Allows Mechanical Rollers to work on moving Sable contraptions.
loconautics.configuration.patch.enablePl: Allows Mechanical Ploughs to work on moving Sable contraptions.
loconautics.configuration.patch.rollerHe: How many blocks above the surface a Mechanical Roller clears.
loconautics.configuration.patch.requireM: Controls whether the Create patches should consume materials for block placement.
loconautics.configuration.gauges.dialWob: Needle wobble in degrees on gauges. Set to 0 to keep the needle steady.
loconautics.ponder.boiler_firebox.text_1: The Firebox burns fuel to heat a Boiler
loconautics.ponder.boiler_firebox.text_2: Right click it with any furnace fuel to light it
loconautics.ponder.boiler_firebox.text_3: It holds a single stack and burns it faster under load
loconautics.ponder.boiler_firebox.text_4: An empty hand will swing the doors open or closed
loconautics.ponder.boiler_firebox.text_5: Using a Shovel scrapes the fire back out
loconautics.ponder.boiler_firebox.text_6: A Firebox Stocker underneath holds 9 stacks of fuel
loconautics.ponder.boiler_assembly.text_: Boiler Body blocks touching the Firebox form the barrel
A Smokestack on top of any body block lets waste gas out
Water enters through a Fluid Hatch touching a body block
A Steam Takeoff against the barrel turns steam into rotation
Engineer's Goggles on the Firebox name the next missing piece
loconautics.ponder.boiler_ratio.text_1: One Firebox can heat 3 Boiler Body blocks
loconautics.ponder.boiler_ratio.text_2: Too much barrel leaves the boiler underfired and below full pressure
loconautics.ponder.boiler_ratio.text_3: Too much fire gains nothing and burns fuel faster
loconautics.ponder.boiler_ratio.text_4: The Efficiency reading shows how well the two match
loconautics.ponder.boiler_smokestack.tex: Waste gas leaves through a Smokestack on any body block
Without a stack, gas builds up in the barrel...
...and chokes the output completely after 45 seconds
Fitting the stack clears the gas twice as fast
The smoke color shows how hot the boiler is running
loconautics.ponder.boiler_water.text_1: A Fluid Hatch against a body block is a water inlet
loconautics.ponder.boiler_water.text_2: Hose Nozzles can dock into it to fill the boiler
loconautics.ponder.boiler_water.text_3: Using a Fluid Pipe on the barrel places a Barrel Pipe Connector
loconautics.ponder.boiler_water.text_4: Pipes alone will not move any water
loconautics.ponder.boiler_water.text_5: A powered Mechanical Pump will push the water in
loconautics.ponder.boiler_water.text_6: The connector only takes water in, it cannot drain the boiler
loconautics.ponder.boiler_takeoff.text_1: Steam Takeoffs against the barrel generate Rotational Force
loconautics.ponder.boiler_takeoff.text_2: Speed follows the pressure, from 4 to 128 RPM
loconautics.ponder.boiler_takeoff.text_3: Stress Capacity depends on the size of the barrel
loconautics.ponder.boiler_takeoff.text_4: Without the boiler, the shaft winds down in 3 seconds
loconautics.ponder.boiler_pressure.text_: A burning, watered boiler builds up pressure
Working pressure is 1.0, and it bursts at 1.6
Safety Valves vent the pressure from the barrel
Right click a Safety Valve with a Valve to bind it
Smart Safety Valves vent by themselves at 3/4 of burst pressure
loconautics.ponder.boiler_failure.text_1: A hot boiler with no water will fail in 30 seconds...
loconautics.ponder.boiler_failure.text_2: ...but refilling it brings the countdown down twice as fast
loconautics.ponder.boiler_failure.text_3: A full fire against a shut valve will burst the barrel
loconautics.ponder.boiler_failure.text_4: Waste gas only chokes the output, it never explodes
loconautics.ponder.boiler_failure.text_5: The blast scales with the size of the barrel
loconautics.ponder.boiler_failure.text_6: In Arcade mode it locks out, and a Shovel resets it
loconautics.ponder.boiler_gauge.text_1: Right click a Firebox with a Locomotive Gauge to bind it
loconautics.ponder.boiler_gauge.text_2: It can be placed on any face in the same level
loconautics.ponder.boiler_gauge.text_3: Using a Wrench on it opens its settings
loconautics.ponder.boiler_gauge.text_4: Gauges also read speedometers, stressometers and fluid valves
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_1: Panels hold up to 4 parts, one in each quadrant
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_2: Aim at a free quadrant to place the next part there
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_3: A lone part sits centered until a second one moves it to a corner
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_4: Using a Wrench configures the part it points at
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_5: Sneak and right click with a Wrench to take a part back
loconautics.ponder.panel_parts.text_6: Breaking the panel takes its parts out one at a time
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_1: Controls are bound to a Redstone Link receiver first
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_2: A Gauge Button sends a full signal for 1 second
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_3: A Gauge Switch holds the signal until it is toggled
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_4: A Gauge Lever is analog, drag it from 0 to 15
loconautics.ponder.panel_controls.text_5: Two controls on one link do not fight, the strongest wins
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_single.h: Generating Rotational Force using Small Combustion Engines
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_single.t: Small Combustion Engines burn liquid fuel to generate Rotational Force
Right click it with a bucket of fuel to fill its tank
Rotational Force will be output through the shaft on its front
At most it provides 256 RPM and 8192 Stress Units
Cerisene is the best fuel, while Lava is the weakest
Engineer's Goggles will show whether it is running or out of fuel
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_pipes.te: Fuel is received through the bottom of the engine
A Fluid Tank and Pipes can supply it
Pipes alone will not move any fuel
Once powered, the pump will push fuel into the engine...
...which will run until the tank is empty
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_tandem.t: Engines placed in a line facing the same way will connect...
...and switch to models that fit together
A row can hold up to 3 Engines
The front Engine outputs the Rotational Force of the whole row
Each running engine adds 8192 Stress Units to the output
Fuel is shared, and a broken engine passes its own on
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_redstone: Without a Redstone signal engines run at full speed
Every point of signal strength slows them by a sixteenth
A signal of 8 leaves half of the speed
At 14 the engines run at their slowest
A signal of 15 will turn them off
A signal at any engine of the row controls the whole row
loconautics.ponder.small_engine_panel.te: Right click an Engine with a Gauge Lever to bind it
Its power acts as a Redstone signal, 15 turns the engine off
A Gauge Switch works the other way round, on is full speed
A Valve is bound the same way
It goes from full speed to the slowest, never off
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_1: Hose Winches attach flat to any block face
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_2: Rotational Force will reel the hose in or out
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_3: One direction pays hose out, the other hauls it back
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_4: A Redstone signal locks the reel like a ratchet
loconautics.ponder.hose_winch.text_5: Breaking the winch snaps the hose and drops the Hose item
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_1: Hose Nozzles are loose bodies, they fall and swing freely
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_2: Right click the winch with a Hose, then the nozzle
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_3: A dotted line previews the run while one end is selected
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_4: The preview turns orange off target and red past 28 blocks
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_5: Sneak and right click to drop the selection
loconautics.ponder.hose_connect.text_6: Once taut a hose cannot stretch, but the winch can pay out more
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_1: Right click a nozzle with an empty hand to hold it
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_2: Scrolling pushes it out or pulls it closer
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_3: Holding Tab while moving the mouse turns it
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_4: Near a Fluid Hatch, a nozzle docks itself upright
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_5: Grabbing a docked nozzle pops it out again
loconautics.ponder.hose_nozzle.text_6: A taut hose pops it out as well
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_1: Hoses need a Mechanical Pump on the face opposite the mount
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_2: Pump speed sets how far the pressure reaches...
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_3: ...up to 28 blocks at the top speed
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_4: Docked, everything pumped goes into the hatch's tank
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_5: It can pull fluid back out the other way too
loconautics.ponder.hose_fluid.text_6: A loose nozzle sprays, and the jet pushes it back
loconautics.ponder.hose_spray.text_1: Water puts out fires and soaks farmland
loconautics.ponder.hose_spray.text_2: Lava lights surfaces and sets mobs alight
loconautics.ponder.hose_spray.text_3: Potions apply their effects to anyone sprayed
loconautics.ponder.hose_spray.text_4: Honey slows down whatever it covers
loconautics.ponder.hose_spray.text_5: Other fluids can be given an effect by a datapack
loconautics.ponder.transmission_single.t: Transmissions relay Rotational Force and set its speed from a signal
Rotational Force enters through the shaft on one end
With no signal the output stays still
A Redstone signal on one side sets the output speed
The output grows with the strength of the signal
At full strength it turns at 256 RPM
loconautics.ponder.transmission_directio: A signal on the opposite side reverses the output
The speed stays the same while the direction flips
loconautics.ponder.transmission_frequenc: Right click it with empty hands to open its Interface
The Speed row is the frequency that sets the output speed
The Direction row is the frequency that reverses it
Redstone Links on the same frequencies now control the Transmission
loconautics.ponder.transmission_panel.te: Sneak and Right click a Transmission with a Gauge Lever to bind it
Dragging the lever sets the speed of the Transmission
A Gauge Switch bound the same way sets the direction
Redstone signals are ignored while a panel drives it
loconautics.ponder.locomotive_wheels.tex: Bearing Axles drive the wheels of the bogey they sit beside
They have to touch the bogey on its rail line, never above or below
A bogey can only be driven by one Bearing Axle
Engineer's Goggles show whether an axle is valid
loconautics.ponder.locomotive_drive.head: Powering Locomotives with Transmissions
loconautics.ponder.locomotive_drive.text: A Transmission goes on the shaft end of the Bearing Axle
A Portable Engine provides the Rotational Force on the other side
Burning fuel in the engine starts the rotation
The Portable Engine is only a demonstration, any Rotational Force works
A Creative Motor can power the Transmission as well
And so can a spinning Water Wheel
A Speed signal decides how fast the Bearing Axle turns
Binding Bearing Axles to Redstone Links
Right click it with empty hands to open its Interface
The Left row is the frequency that steers the train left
The Right row is the frequency that steers it right
Each frequency is made of two Items, like a Redstone Link
loconautics.ponder.locomotive_controls.t: Analog Controllers send the signals that drive a locomotive
Sneak and Right click it to open its Interface
Speed and Direction are the frequencies the Transmission listens to
Left and Right are the frequencies the Bearing Axle listens to
Right click a Controller while Sneaking to copy them onto a block
Sneak and Right click in the air to clear the copied frequencies
loconautics.ponder.locomotive_assembly.t: A locomotive needs a Bearing Axle and a Transmission on its bogey
Right click the Station to open its Interface
The New Train button switches the Station to Assembly mode
Assemble as Sable Train builds the locomotive as a physics train
Raising the Analog Controller output steps the train up to speed
Letting go steps the output and the train back down
Hold Space near a Station to park the train on it
A Physics Assembler can also turn a train back into blocks
loconautics.ponder.analog_controller_int: Analog Controllers send throttle and steering over Redstone Link frequencies
Right click one to take control of it
Holding forward raises the output one level at a time
Letting go steps the output back down
Sprint locks the output where it is
The mouse wheel sets the highest level the output can reach
loconautics.ponder.analog_controller_fre: Binding Analog Controllers to Redstone Links
Sneak and Right click it to open its Interface
The Speed row is the frequency sent while driving forward
The Direction row is the one sent while driving backward
The Left row is the frequency sent while steering left
The Right row is the frequency sent while steering right
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_ass: Turntable Bearings attach to the block in front of them
Use Super Glue to select the blocks that will turn with it
Right click the bearing to assemble them
A cogwheel beside the bearing sets how fast it turns
Each Redstone pulse turns it by a set angle
It holds that angle until the next pulse
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_ins: Sneak and Right click it to open its Interface
Turn rotates the structure by an exact angle, up to a full circle
The arrows next to an angle set the direction and double the speed
Delay holds it still for a set time
Await pauses the list until the next Redstone signal
The list stops at End and starts over on the next signal
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_tri: This behavior can be configured using the value panel
Pulse runs the list once for each signal
Repeat While Powered starts the list again until the signal ends
Alternate Direction flips the turn with every signal
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_sch: Setting the first instruction to Schedule lets Train Schedules turn the structure
Rails on it meet the rails of the legs around it
A Train carrying a Schedule for the other leg parks centered on it
It turns the Train to face that leg, no Redstone needed
Then the Train drives off and it turns back to where it started
The cogwheel needs Rotational Force and the structure has to be as long as the Train
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_dia: Reaching Diagonal Legs with Turntable Bearings
A Turntable can turn to any angle, so a leg can leave it diagonally
A Train whose Schedule needs the diagonal leg parks centered on the plate
The plate turns it by whatever angle that leg needs
Then the Train drives straight onto the diagonal leg
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_sig: Binding Train Signals to Turntable Bearings
Sneak and Right click a Turntable Bearing with a Train Signal to bind it
Signals placed afterwards are linked to that bearing
Linked signals stay red while the plate is turning or holds a Train
They turn green again once the plate has settled
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_par: Stations on different legs can share one name, with a * to match them all
A Train sent to that name takes a station that is free
The Turntable turns it toward the leg that has a free station
The Train parks there and the plate returns to its first angle
loconautics.ponder.turntable_bearing_man: Leaving a Parking with Turntable Bearings
A Train parked on a dead end leg has to back out when its Schedule moves on
The plate turns to meet the leg the Train waits on
A Maneuver instruction goes into the Schedule between two destinations
Its speed is a share of full speed, up to 75 percent
The destination after it is where the Train maneuvers to, so it needs one
The Train reverses out of the parking at that speed
It stops centered on the plate
The plate takes the Train and turns it to face the leg it needs next
Then it drives off forward toward its next stop
loconautics.ponder.train_casing_bogeys.t: Holding C with a Train Casing opens the selection menu
Scrolling swaps the Casing for a Bogey
Right click a Track to place the Bogey on it
Train Casings placed between the Bogeys form the body of the train
Glue the blocks together and hold right click on a Physics Assembler
The assembled body counts as a Train and can dock at Stations
loconautics.ponder.train_casing_shaft.te: Bogeys can be fitted with a Shaft by right clicking them with one
Rotation from one side passes straight through, like an encased Shaft
Sneak and Right click with a Wrench to remove the Shaft again
Without the Shaft, rotation stops at the Bogey
